title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Besides hailing from Astora, little is known about Andre; he seems to cherish dependability, which might vaguely suggest a history of betrayal, though this is never elaborated upon. He is also acquainted with the Giant Blacksmith, as evidenced when he notices the player holding the Giant's Coal.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Andre's stocky build, beard, dour demeanor and profession as a blacksmith of legendary weapons resembles popular depictions of the *dwarves*, originally of Norse myth, and later popularized by the works of Tolkien and *Dungeons & Dragons*.
**Andre's name is similar to that of the dwarf *Andvari* of Norse myth.
**Bodies of blacksmiths closely resembling Andre are found in various locations, seemingly petrified. In Norse myth, dwarves are said to be turned to stone by sunlight. Two of the petrified dwarves in Dark Souls are located in ruined buildings which appear to have been exposed to sunlight due to structural damage.
**Dwarves in Norse myth are famed for the creation of magic items, particularly magic weapons of unparalleled strength. These include Thor's hammer *Mjolnir*, Odin's spear *Gungnir*, the reforged sword *Gram*, and the cursed sword *Tyrfing*.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Often the first blacksmith new players come across, Andre of Astora can be a welcome sight. Andre of Astora is the only blacksmith that can ascend weapons down the Standard path from +5 to +6 and from +10 to +11. He is also the only blacksmith that can ascend weapons down the Raw, Divine and Occult paths.

He also sells some basic upgrade materials, as well as many weapons (some of which are unique to him). Finally, he sells the Crest of Artorias, which is required to open the door to Darkroot Forest, a more dangerous section of Darkroot Garden.

In *Dark Souls III*, he acts as the blacksmith in Firelink Shrine. At the beginning he is unable to infuse weapons without the correspondent coals found through the game to expand his services. Once the player has found a coal, returning it to him will unlock new infusion options.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre has a west country accent, a region in the UK famous as the supposed birthplace of King Arthur. While it's likely a choice of actor, the fact remains he is one of the few with a true regional English accent. Notably, the west country is frequently depicted/stereotyped as the countryside in media. The line by Rickert, "an old smith out in the country", may allude to Andre.
Andre is one of the few characters that do not disintegrate when killed. This may be because he uses a unique model, or perhaps signifies he is not an Undead or monster.
It was originally intended that Andre was to be a descendant of Gwyn and that he would have a key role in the story, but this idea was scrapped.
Andre is one of the few characters in *Dark Souls* whose mouth moves when he speaks (the others being Quelaag's Sister, Kingseeker Frampt, Alvina and Darkstalker Kaathe).

 lead : **Andre of Astora** (アストラのアンドレイ) is a character in *Dark Souls*. He is a blacksmith that will likely prove invaluable to the player throughout the game. Andre is voiced by Sean Barrett, who also voiced Ingward and Petrus of Thorolund.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : Despite what common sense might dictate, Andre does not use his hammer to fight, preferring to simply use his bare hands. This certainly does not mean that he is a pushover, however; his heavier punches can knock players off their feet, while his jabs are fast and can quickly deal a lot of damage. Andre has a roster of moves unique to him, including a drop kick that has heavy knockback and deals high damage. He also sports unusually high health for a character of his stature, so it may take a while to wear him down.

title: Anor Londo
snippet:
If the player is killed whilst in darkened Anor Londo, they are returned to the first bonfire regardless of whether they have rested there or not. Whether it is a glitch or an intended function by the developers is unconfirmed.

If the player desires to fight Dark Sun Gwyndolin via an easy return to the boss area, it is preferable to either:
Leave Gwynevere alive so as to not make Anor Londo dark, and then fight Gwyndolin. This allows the player to respawn at the Darkmoon Tomb bonfire.
After killing Gwynevere, ignore the Darkmoon Knightess (so as not to kill her in combat) to keep the first Bonfire lit so that the player may warp to the Darkmoon Tomb after death.

If the player has already darkened Anor Londo and killed the Darkmoon Knightess, the fastest method will be to run to the entrance way of The Duke's Archives (only accessible after placing the Lordvessel) and using the bonfire by the elevator to warp.

title: Backstep
snippet:
During the backstep, from frame 11 to 14, the player has hyperarmor, i.e. infinite poise. That means, no matter what hits the player, they will not stumble and stay on their feet. For example, the player can backstep through the boulders in Sen's Fortress without being knocked down. Keep in mind that you will still take damage, since the hyperarmor frames do not grant invincibility. The backwards ninja flip does not have hyperarmor frames.
When inputing an attack directly after the backstep, the player will perform a running attack. This can be very useful in combat, by dodging an enemy's attack with the backstep, then striking back with a running attack.

title: Backstep
snippet:
Backstep -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : Backstepping is a gameplay mechanic in Dark Souls.

A backstep is performed by pressing the roll key without pressing in any direction. The player will then take a leap backwards instead of rolling.

Backstepping also grants invincibility frames, but fewer than rolling. While rolling gives 11 i-frames, backsteps only give 4. Equipping the Dark Wood Grain Ring replaces the backstep with a backwards ninja flip with 8 i-frames. This may now seem like backstepping is generally worse that rolling. However, backstepping has two situational advantages over rolling.

Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : Gargoyles are stone creatures created by the Gods through magic to help patrol Anor Londo or sites deemed important. In addition to their tough and hard skin, they are able to breathe fire or lightning and are armed with a bronze shield and a bronze helmet for purely decorative purposes while they use a bronze halberd as a weapon.

After Lord Gwyn sacrificed himself to link the First Flame and prolong the Age of Fire, several Gargoyles were placed to guard the Bell of Awakening placed on the Undead Church of the Undead Burg and act as ritual challenge. The Undead who wished to follow in Gwyn's footsteps to sacrifice themselves to the Flame would have to be tested before obtaining the Lordvessel and seeking powerful souls. Ringing the Bells of Awakening represents only the first of these challenges, and success means gaining access to Sen's Fortress to be tested further.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : In human form, it is possible to have Solaire of Astora and/or Knight Lautrec of Carim assist during this battle, although Lautrec must be freed and spoken to in Firelink Shrine first. Their summon signs are found just before the white light leading to the Gargoyles. Summoning both knights and simply mobbing each Gargoyle can lead to a quick and relatively painless victory.

The fight is beset by the constant danger of falling off (target-locking, coupled with the camera angle and narrow field of view, can make it hard to track the player character's footing) and facing off against a single gargoyle on top of the church roof. Trying to circle the gargoyle while holding up a shield is a good way to avoid its long-reaching frontal attacks. If the gargoyle takes off, move away or get ready to dodge its plunging attack.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - location 
 location : On top of the church in the Undead Parish, reached by passing through the room full of hollows and a Channeler, before climbing two ladders and finally entering the fog gate. They are also found in Anor Londo as mini-bosses: Exit the first bonfire, go straight on and down the lift, and a gargoyle will be straight ahead. The second is beyond the rotating staircase-bridge.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Once the first gargoyle is cut down to half its health, the second gargoyle will join the fight. Fortunately, this gargoyle is already severely injured (it arrives at half-health). It has the same attacks as the first gargoyle minus those that involve flying or using the tail.

Players having difficulty managing their positioning against the two gargoyles should save any consumables (ex., Fire Bombs) until the first gargoyle's health is approaching 50%, and then use them to finish it off as quickly as possible. For as long as both gargoyles are alive, players should keep them both on the screen; if not feasible, one can try following audio cues to perceive an oncoming attack. The use of Gold Pine Resin and other weapon enhancements can greatly help in finishing off the first gargoyle, and make the overall fight significantly easier.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Both Gargoyles wield halberds and can breathe fire, although the first gargoyle usually will only breathe fire after the second one jumps down. A fire-resistant shield such as the Black Knight Shield (and, optionally, fire-resistant armor) can be very useful, as the fire breath covers a wide area. While breathing fire, the gargoyles won't move, making it the perfect opportunity to run over and hit them from behind (this makes avoiding or blocking the fire twice as important, as its stagger effect will consume precious seconds, limiting the time available to attack the gargoyles).

The first gargoyle's tail can be severed to gain a weapon (Gargoyle Tail Axe).

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - quelaag_s_domain_bell 
 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - trivia 
 trivia : The Japanese description of Seath's Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard uses the term (Hepburn: *gaiseki*) 'consort kin', which is used to define a person related by marriage to the maternal clan or wife's clan of the monarch, thus stating how Seath had become part of Gwyn's family through marriage with one of the daughters of his mother. However, if interpreted differently by reading the individual kanji separately like 外 (Gai) and 戚 (Seki), it would be translated as "external relative", implying that Seath would have married any woman from Gwyn's family.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet: **While the term has a historical and cultural meaning too complex to properly convey in the context of the game's lore and the fact that one could become a "Gaiseki" even marrying a sibling or cousin of the monarch's mother or even by having the monarch marry one's daughter, it is more likely that Gwyn gave Seath one of his daughters as a gift thus allowing the dragon a more close connection to the family of the monarch.

title: Dark Lord
snippet: The interpretation of the Dark Lord's role in founding a new world order seems to have varied over time. The "Dark Lord" ending of *Dark Souls I* entails abandoning the First Flame to die out and beginning a new age from naught; the "Usurpation of Fire" ending of *Dark Souls III* however is somewhat different. Many millennia past the time of the Chosen Undead, the Sable Church of Londor, founded by three sisters who were disciples of Kaathe, are searching for a worthy Lord of Men. If the Ashen One cooperates with Yuria, a sister of the Sable Church, they are asked to "usurp the Flame", to "wrest it from its mantle". In doing so, the Ashen One would inherit what little lifeforce remains of the First Flame, and thus become a worthy Lord of Men—that is, a "Lord of Hollows", as it has come to be referred to. title: Boss (Dark Souls II)

Boss (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : A **boss** is a powerful, non-respawning enemy in *Dark Souls II*. Bosses are distinguishable from normal enemies as their name and health are displayed at the bottom of the screen once encountered, and they are usually on the opposite side of a white fog door.

In addition to bosses, there are a number of enemies that don't respawn upon death and are sometimes referred to as *minibosses*.

Unlike the bosses found in *Dark Souls*, the majority of bosses found in *Dark Souls II* can be considered optional, due to the Shrine of Winter's flexible requirements for passing. The list of bosses below is treated under the assumption that the player takes the most linear route, collecting the four Lord Souls, and at least passes through each major location.

title: Pyromancer
snippet:
Pyromancer -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Pyromancer** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls*.

Pyromancers combine early access to Pyromancy with decent physical damage. Pyromancers are also unique in that they start at Level 1, so they possess the advantage of being able to invade any person at the start, as well as keeping at the lowest level possible. These factors make the Pyromancer a good choice for PvP builds.

The Pyromancer has quite a few advantages early in the game, including the ability to combine reasonably strong melee attacks from the Hand Axe with very potent Fireball pyromancy. Their starting armor, while decrepit looking, actually has strong resistance to both Poison and Fire, which are common hazards in the early areas of the game.

Pyromancers do, however, start with the worst shield in the game, although it is still reasonably effective up until the point where a player can obtain a better one.

 lead : **Bosses** are significant enemies in *Dark Souls III*. They usually control access to other areas throughout the game. Many bosses are mandatory for the completion of the main quest line, and some are optional.

Upon defeat, most bosses drop individual souls specific to themselves. These may be consumed or sold to acquire a large quantity of souls or may be transposed by Ludleth of Courland for weapons, shields, rings, miracles, pyromancies, or sorceries.

Once an area boss has been defeated, cooperation with friendly phantoms is disabled. However, the player will still be able to summon dark spirits and mad phantoms for PvP.

There are also minibosses in the game that do not respawn once killed. For the purposes of this wiki, those minibosses who drop a unique itemized soul are included in this article.

 characteristics : As with its predecessor, the Dark Sword mainly performs wide sweeping attacks like the Broadsword (with exception being the rolling attacks). It is somewhat heavier than most other straight swords, such as the Long Sword. It scales best with Strength, and due to its early availability it makes a good choice for an early game weapon.

What sets the Dark Sword apart from its peers, however, is its skill, Stomp, which is a skill normally only seen on greatswords and ultra greatswords. Using the skill will grant the wielder Hyper Armor, something that is otherwise only seen on heavier weapons, allowing players to trade against opponents wielding similarly-sized weaponry.

The in-game location is at the heart of the New Londo Ruins, a featureless expanse where the Chosen Undead must slay the Four Kings and can encounter Darkstalker Kaathe. title: New Game Plus (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
New Game Plus (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - differences 
 differences : Upon starting New Game+, the game will restart from the beginning with the world, including area progression, story events, and lootable items, fully reset. The player keeps all their non-story based weapons, armor, items, and rings; and retains their soul level, stats, and covenant standings.

Upon entering New Game+, enemies receive a substantial increase to their health and damage output, but also reward more souls upon their defeat. Furthermore, Bosses will drop their specific souls when killed, allowing the player to either transpose the items they did not obtain in their first New Game cycle, or duplicates of items they already obtained. This notably allows a player to transpose the Twin Princes' Greatsword without having another player drop one of the swords during online play.

One of four great beings who must be slain in *Dark Souls* so that their special souls may satiate the Lordvessel, he uniquely has two distinct boss battles, each with a different location and moveset. title: Varangian Armor
snippet:

 characteristics : The Varangian Armor is light and easily acquired, and offers more defense than other light chest pieces. The most notable advantage it gives is favorable early-game Poison resistance, which can be helpful later, especially in The Gutter and in the Black Gulch.

title: Torch

title: Gods Grave
snippet:
Gods Grave -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - environment 
 environment : While having no textures or objects, rudimentary level geometry contained in the map data for Dark Souls 3 resembles the Catacombs from Dark Souls 1 and/or the section of Lost Izalith containing the Bed of Chaos. Despite no assets pertaining to the area itself, references to the area are found in data strings within objects that were later used within the Ringed City: the gravestones located in the first section of the Ringed City that block arrows from the archers, and strange pots which have roots growing out of them.

This being said, it is known that the top half of the area was in a forest, for standard trees present in various areas of the final game are also present here.

What was in the bottom half of the area is still unknown.

title: Critical attack
snippet:
Critical attack -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Critical attacks** (also known as **critical hits** or just **criticals**) are a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls*, *Dark Souls II* and *Dark Souls III*. Critical attacks are performed in what is considered the most vulnerable areas of enemies. There are four types of critical attacks: backstabs, ripostes, headshots and plunging attacks.

title: Boss
snippet:
Boss -  Dark Souls - boss - lead 
 lead : A **boss** is a powerful, non-respawning enemy in *Dark Souls*. Bosses are distinguishable from normal enemies as their name and HP are displayed at the bottom of the screen once encountered, and they are usually on the opposite side of a white fog door.

While players will generally end up fighting most of the bosses, not all of them need to be killed in order to beat the game.

In addition to bosses, there are a number of enemies that don't respawn upon death and are sometimes referred to as minibosses.

title: Demon Ruins
snippet:
Demon Ruins -  Dark Souls - location - location 
 location : Found shortly after Quelaag's Domain. The Demon Ruins lead to Lost Izalith; however, Lost Izalith cannot be accessed until the player has retrieved the Lordvessel from Anor Londo and placed it in the Firelink Altar.

On arrival, most of the area is flooded with lava until the Ceaseless Discharge is slain. Once the lava is drained, the lower section of the area may be accessed, and it is here that the route to Lost Izalith lies, initially blocked by the Lordvessel-related orange fog gate.

The area just after the Demon Firesage has an elevator that will transport the player back up to the Bell of Awakening in Queelag's Domain.

title: New Game Plus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
New Game Plus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - overview 
 overview : The story and events in New Game Plus are identical to New Game. The player keeps all weapons, armor, rings, and consumable items that they have acquired, unless said items are plot-critical. They also retain their soul level, stats, and covenant standings. The primary differences are an increase in game difficulty, in the form of more powerful enemies, and greater soul gains from defeating these stronger enemies. New enemies are also introduced, often in the form of black phantom versions of enemies that normally appear in that area. Additionally, some corpses and chests contain different items, certain bosses gain additional drops, and some fights are changed through the addition of new mechanics, attacks, or additional enemies.

title: Witch Beatrice
snippet:

As *Dark Souls* is heavily influenced by *Berserk*, it is possible that Child Beatrice is related to the character Schierke, as both are children, both are witches, wear similar attire and both are normally seen holding a staff.

title: Archdrake Staff
snippet:
Archdrake Staff -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics

title: Lordvessel
snippet:
Lordvessel -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Upon acquiring the Lordvessel, players can warp to select bonfires. Players must rest at a bonfire in order to use the warping ability. It is possible to warp from any bonfire, excluding the ones in the Painted World of Ariamis, The Duke's Archives, Prison Tower (though this bonfire can actually be warped from if you use it from *outside* the cell), and the Undead Burg. Extinguished bonfires can still be warped to.

Under the guidance of either Darkstalker Kaathe or Kingseeker Frampt, the player may place the Lordvessel at the Firelink Altar. In doing so, boss areas containing the Lord Souls and Bequeathed Lord Soul Shards will become accessible. Once the Lordvessel is satiated, the doors to the Kiln of the First Flame are made open, where they may finally face the Lord of Cinder. Players still have the ability to warp, even after placing the Lordvessel.

title: Waterlogged
snippet:
Waterlogged -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Waterlogged** is a status effect in *Dark Souls II*.

It is contracted when standing in a Pharros' Contraption that fills an empty pool with healing water, or patches of water found in many areas of the game. The healing water slowly regenerates health as the player stands in it, and cures status effects like poison by allowing it to wash off. This effect also works like the Flash Sweat pyromancy, making the player far more resistant to fire attacks, at the cost of taking more lightning damage. The effect can also stack with Flash Sweat for even more fire defense.

In some areas of the game, this can occur automatically, such as traversing water itself, or during a rain storm. However, this will not regenerate the player's health, but instead only alter their elemental resistances. Care should be taken as to who or what the player is going to fight when the status effect is contracted.

 straid_s_cell : There are five Undead Citizens immediately outside the Straid's Cell bonfire in the Lost Bastille. title: Dark Souls II
snippet:
Dark Souls II -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : ***Dark Souls II*** is a fantasy action-RPG game developed by From Software and is a follow up to *Dark Souls*. It was announced on December 7, 2012. The game has been published for the PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and PC by Namco Bandai Games. *Dark Souls II* was released on the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 on March 11, 2014 in North America, on March 13th in Japan and Australia and on March 14th in Europe. The PC version was released on April 25th, 2014. The game has a sequel, *Dark Souls III*, which was released in 2016.

title: Firebomb (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Firebomb (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - item - general_information 
 general_information : When used, the Firebomb is thrown a fair distance, and explodes on the first thing it makes contact with, dealing Fire damage in a small area. The damage may be increased by improving the player's Fire bonus, which is increased by improving one or both of Intelligence and Faith.

Early in the game, Firebombs perform exceptionally well against many enemy types, while being both easy and cheap to get. Later in the game, they are outperformed by Black Firebombs.

snippet:

title: Dark Hand (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Dark Hand (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Returning from the first game, the Dark Hand can be useful as an early-game weapon but otherwise functions as a utility tool.

Unlike other fist weapons, the Dark Hand is not paired, and it cannot be two-handed. Wielding the weapon in different hands results in different movesets. In the right-hand, it functions as a one-handed fist weapon, performing various close-combat attacks; in the left-hand, it can be used to project a shield that has high elemental defense but low stability, making it ideal for protecting the wielder against projectile spells, as well as perform a unique skill.

Because it cannot be upgraded, the Dark Hand ceases to be useful later in the game when higher-damage weapons become available. However, because it has high base Dark damage, it is very effective in the early game.
